content_preview.title: pg_clickhouse 0.11.1 Adds pgvector Pushdown and Lightweight UPDATE, DELETE on ClickHouse Foreign Tables
content_preview.summary: The ClickHouse-maintained Postgres extension now pushes pgvector distance searches, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, and nine regression functions down to ClickHouse foreign tables.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

ClickHouse has released version 0.11.1 of pg_clickhouse, the PostgreSQL extension it maintains for offloading analytic queries from a Postgres database to a connected ClickHouse server, adding pushdown support for pgvector similarity search, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `TRUNCATE` operations, and nine linear-regression aggregate functions. The release was published on [GitHub](https://github.com/ClickHouse/pg_clickhouse/releases/tag/v0.11.1) on November 9, 2026, and covered on the [Click...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean News-format writeup of a dot release. Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Analysis structure is well organized, every bullet in 'What We Know' carries an inline attribution, and the lede correctly frames pg_clickhouse as the extension ClickHouse maintains rather than implying ClickHouse itself is the database being extended.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both snapshots in sources/2026-11/pg_clickhouse-0111-adds-pgvector-pushdown-and-lightweight-update-delete-on-clickhouse-foreign-tables/ were decompressed and read in full (source-0.html.gz = GitHub releases/tag/v0.11.1, 200 OK, sha256 264a6cb0... verified by rehash; source-1.html.gz = clickhouse.com/blog/pg-clickhouse-0-11-1, 200 OK, sha256 31455d7b... verified by rehash). manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for both — no injection scan hits. Every claim in 'What We Know' was checked line-by-line against the raw extracted text: pgvector column mapping (Array(Float32)/Float64/BFloat16, = and <> pushdown) matches GitHub bullet verbatim; distance operators <->, <=>, <#>, <+> plus l2_distance/cosine_distance/inner_product/l1_distance/vector_dims and the ClickHouse 23.8+ gate for <#> match GitHub verbatim; EXPLAIN vector-index reporting and pg_clickhouse.vector_planner_warnings match GitHub verbatim and are corroborated by the blog's worked EXPLAIN example (Vector Index / Vector Index Not Used lines); UPDATE/DELETE on MergeTree foreign tables, the RETURNING/joins/Postgres-condition fallback-to-error behavior, and the ClickHouse 25.7+ gate match GitHub verbatim and are corroborated by the blog's worked UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE walkthrough; TRUNCATE support matches both; the nine regr_* functions (avgx, avgy, count, intercept, r2, slope, sxx, sxy, syy) and the ClickHouse 26.9+ gate match both sources exactly, count of nine confirmed by listing; jsonb subscript pushdown to dot notation and the new 'settings' option for foreign servers/tables match GitHub verbatim; the HTTP-to-binary default driver change and the session_settings override-by-key behavior match GitHub verbatim. The direct quote 'delivers a slew of improvements and bug fixes, including' is verbatim from the blog's opening paragraph ('...pg_clickhouse v0.11.1, released last week, delivers a slew of improvements and bug fixes, including UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, and pgvector search pushdown') — I independently re-checked this against the raw snapshot text myself; it is a real, exact sentence fragment, not a hallucination, and the article uses only the quoted fragment inside quote marks while the unquoted continuation ('UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, and pgvector search pushdown') also matches the source's own continuation. No other direct quotes appear in the body. Dates verified: GitHub shows the release as 'released this 09 Nov 15:30' (matches article's November 9, 2026) and the blog is bylined 'David Wheeler, Nov 19, 2026' (matches article's November 19 citation); both snapshots carry 2026 contextual dates elsewhere on the page (e.g. blog's own November 2026 newsletter teaser, '© 2026 ClickHouse'), consistent with the article's year. Both sources are vendor-controlled (ClickHouse's own GitHub org and ClickHouse's own blog) — acceptable for News-category release coverage, which carries no independent-sourcing requirement (that requirement applies only to Analysis), but noted for the record: 0 of 2 sources are independent of the subject. Follow-up/originality check: read the archive's existing article at src/content/articles/2026-08/21-pg_clickhouse-v010-pushes-correlated-subqueries-to-clickhouse-cutting-a-tpc-h-query-from-327-seconds-to-37-milliseconds.md in full. Confirmed this is a genuine, non-duplicate follow-up: the v0.10 article's 'What We Don't Know' section states ClickHouse's post 'does not give a timeline... for the broader roadmap items it lists as still open, including lightweight DELETE/UPDATE pushdown and UNION pushdown' — this submission's Analysis section accurately states that lightweight DELETE/UPDATE pushdown 'was reported as a still-open roadmap item when version 0.10 shipped in August' and that 0.11.1 'closes it.' Note for the orchestrator: the submission does NOT claim pgvector pushdown itself was flagged 'still open' in the v0.10 article (it wasn't — the v0.10 piece never mentions vector search); the submission correctly and precisely describes vector similarity search as 'a new category' introduced in 0.11.1, distinct from the DELETE/UPDATE item that was explicitly on the v0.10 roadmap. This is the accurate reading of both articles, not an error. No other published article in src/content/articles/2026-11/ or elsewhere covers pg_clickhouse 0.11.1. Internal links to the August article (/article/2026-08/21-pg_clickhouse-v010-...) resolve to an existing file. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article's subject is ClickHouse/pg_clickhouse; Anthropic is not referenced as subject, headline, summary, or lead, and contributor_model attribution is handled by the standard pipeline field, not an in-body credit line.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabrications, no misattributions, no hallucinated quotes found. Every specific (version gates, operator lists, function names, release dates, driver default change) traces to one or both cited sources. No absence/quantifier claim ('neither... gives a timeline', 'nine... functions') overstates what the sources actually say.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, technical, no editorializing. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Genuine follow-up to the August v0.10 article, not a duplicate — see source_verification for the specific roadmap-continuity check performed.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced News release writeup; both sources were read in full and every claim traced cleanly, the one direct quote is verbatim, and the follow-up relationship to the August v0.10 article is accurate rather than duplicative. Featured candidacy: 1 - a dot release that adds genuinely new capability (pgvector pushdown, write-statement pushdown) relevant to a defined developer audience running Postgres alongside ClickHouse, but a single-vendor extension update rather than broad-audience or exceptional news.
